title: Add annotate_milestone() — vertical reference line with label
description:
A vertical reference line marking an event (product launch, policy change, COVID lockdown) with a label. Common in business time series.

```r
# Proposed API
ggplot(data, aes(x = date, y = revenue)) +
  geom_line() +
  annotate_milestone(x = as.Date("2024-03-15"), label = "Product launch")
```

Simpler than the other two functions — no data lookup needed, just an x position and a label. Should follow the same styling conventions (arrow, label box, `...` pass-through).

title: Add colorblind-safe default palette option
description:
The default green/red colors for increase/decrease are not colorblind-safe (red-green colorblindness affects ~8% of men).

The `colors` argument already lets users pass custom palettes, so this is about providing a good built-in alternative — likely blue/orange.

**Options:**
- A `colorblind = TRUE` argument that swaps the default palette.
- A package-level option: `options(ggmemo.colorblind = TRUE)`.
- A named palette: `colors = ggmemo_palette("colorblind")`.

This is a self-contained change — good for a first contribution.

title: Pass ... to both segment and label layers in annotate_change()
description:
Currently `...` in `annotate_change()` only reaches the label layer. A user passing `linewidth = 1` expecting a thicker arrow gets nothing — the parameter is silently ignored.

**Options to explore:**
- Split into `label_args` and `segment_args` named list arguments.
- Pass `...` to both layers (may produce ggplot2 warnings for irrelevant params).
- Add specific named arguments for common segment overrides (e.g., `arrow_linewidth`).

See `inst/notes/v0.2-prompt.md` for full design context.

title: Remove x/y column guessing — accept explicit mapping or infer from plot
description:
`detect_x_column()` and `estimate_nudge()` guess which column is x and which is y from the data frame structure. This works on simple 2-column datasets and breaks on wide ones (economics, txhousing).

**Options to explore:**
- Add an explicit `x` parameter: `annotate_change(data, x = quarter, from = ..., to = ..., value = revenue)`.
- If #1 (data inheritance) is solved, extract the x mapping from the plot's `aes()`.
- Accept `mapping = aes(x = quarter, y = revenue)` as in the original DESIGN.md spec.

This is closely related to #1 — solving data inheritance may make the heuristic unnecessary.

See `inst/notes/v0.2-prompt.md` for full design context.

title: Eliminate data redundancy — make data optional or inherited from the plot
description:
Users currently pass `data` to both `ggplot()` and `annotate_*()`:

```r
ggplot(revenue, aes(x = quarter, y = revenue)) +
  geom_col() +
  annotate_change(revenue, from = ..., to = ..., value = revenue)
```

`revenue` appears twice. Every other ggplot2 layer inherits data from the plot — our functions are the exception. This is the most common source of confusion and the biggest barrier to feeling "native" in ggplot2.

**Options to explore:**
- Make `data` optional. If omitted, extract data from the plot object (may require converting to proper ggplot2 Stat/Geom subclasses).
- Accept a plot object as the first argument.
- Keep the current API but document the rationale clearly.

**Constraint:** Whatever approach must still work when added with `+`.

See `inst/notes/v0.2-prompt.md` for full design context.
